questions.question: What kind of language is HTML?
options: A markup language for the structure of a page.
A stylesheet language that paints colors and fonts.
A programming language with functions and loops.
A query language for selecting rows from a table.
questions.explanation: HTML marks up content. CSS styles it. JavaScript programs it. The first chapter is structure, not color.

questions.question: Where do attributes go?
options: On the opening tag, as name="value".
After the element, as a sibling <attr>.
questions.explanation: Attributes appear on the opening tag. Name, equals, double-quoted value.

questions.question: What belongs in <body>?
options: The page title on the browser tab.
Content shown in the main browser window.
Comments the visitor never sees, exclusively.
questions.explanation: Everything inside body is shown inside the main browser window. The title lives in head.

options: Information about the page, such as <title>.
questions.explanation: head contains information about the page rather than what is shown in the main window.

questions.explanation: html is the root. head (with title) comes before body.

options: HTML is only for color and fonts.
Structure helps readers understand the page, the way headings help in a document.
Browsers ignore tags and show the source.

The character encoding of the file.
